sections.h2: Who sends your Wake County tax bill
sections.html:
Wake County Tax Administration sets values and collects payment. Its help desk answers at 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.

A single bill can carry several charges. Under a local agreement the county also collects for the towns and special districts inside its borders, so questions about a town's own rate go to that town hall.

If your lender pays from escrow, no bill is mailed to you. Check the amount online anyway, because as the seller you should know the actual figure.

Commissioners adopted a $2.28 billion budget on June 1 for Fiscal Year 2027. A 2-cent increase lifts the county rate to 53.71 cents. That covers the county share only, and town and district rates are added on top.

The county's own illustration is a $90 increase for the owner of a $450,000 home. For your parcel, ask Tax Administration.

Wake County rate and payment points
TopicDetail
County budget, Fiscal Year 2027$2.28 billion, adopted June 1
Rate changeUp 2 cents to 53.71 cents
Municipal and district chargesCollected by the county on one bill
Pay without interestFull balance by January 5, 2027
Payment plansShort-term plans; any partial payment accepted before the deadline

Bills are due September 1, and January 5 is the last no-interest day. State law adds 2 percent from January 6, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part month from February 1.

The county is flexible before that date. You can pay in pieces of any size with no approval, as long as the balance clears by January 5, and each payment brings a statement of what remains. Short-term plans exist too, and earlier calls get better options. Once a bill turns overdue, the office cannot help, and state law allows collection from wages, accounts or rent.

  • Pay online by bank draft, digital wallet or card.
  • Escrow accounts: the lender pays and no bill arrives.
  • Questions about a bill: 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.

sections.h2: Which value the September 2027 bill uses
sections.html:
The bill due September 1, 2027 uses values as of January 1, 2027, and rates approved by elected officials in June 2027. The bill due September 1, 2026 rests on January 1, 2024 values and the rates approved in June 2026.

A tax bill is two numbers multiplied together: assessed value and the rate per $100 set by county and municipal officials. The county's own worked example uses a house assessed at $450,000 at the 53.71 cent county rate. A revaluation changes values, not rates.

State law also makes local governments publish a revenue-neutral rate during the budget process, meaning the rate that would bring in about the same revenue as before the revaluation. Officials are not required to adopt that rate.

Every two years from here. The commissioners voted in March 2025 to phase in a two-year cycle, with the first two-year revaluation effective January 1, 2029. The idea is that long gaps let increases pile up and land on owners as one sudden jump.

Thirty-seven counties, Wake among them, have revaluations effective January 1, 2027. A rulebook called the Schedule of Values, approved by the commissioners, sets the rates and ranges used to value property between revaluations, and the county posts the PDF at wake.gov/sov.

  • Look up your current assessed value at wake.gov/realestate.
  • Report wrong property data at wake.gov/rehelp, with your address or account number and any documents.
  • Expect occasional appraiser visits: badges, county-marked vehicles, usually 15 to 30 minutes, and photos of the exterior.

sections.h2: Tax Administration address and phone numbers
sections.html:
The office is at 301 S. McDowell St., Ste. 3800, Raleigh, NC 27601. Mail goes to P.O. Box 2331, Raleigh, NC 27602. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding county holidays.

  • Property tax: 919-856-5400. Fax: 919-856-7128.
  • Gross receipts: 919-856-5999.
  • Online help center and chat: taxhelp.wake.gov/hc, or taxhelp@wake.gov.
  • Revaluation and appraisers: 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

The county also runs a Residential Sales Search tool that can filter by distance, sale date, heated area and year built, and a comparable sales tool is planned for January 2027. A seller preparing for a buyer or an appeal can use these listings to see what nearby houses sold for.

sections.h2: What the 2027 revaluation means for a seller
sections.html:
Values reset January 1, 2027, replacing the January 1, 2024 set, and later resets follow every two years. Buyers in 2027 will be pricing the tax on the new number.

The aim is for each assessed value to match fair market value, the most probable open-market price. Work runs through neighborhooding, pricing from sales, field and office review, then notices and appeals. About 460,000 parcels fall into 5,400 neighborhoods.

  • Results go to the commissioners on January 19, 2027, and notices follow that week.
  • The planned appeal deadline is April 30, 2027.

These are published targets. Confirm them at 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

Appeals go to the county's Board of Equalization and Review. Notices of value go out first, and owners can then appeal informally.

State law sets the board's first meeting between the first Mondays of April and May, and a hearing request must arrive before adjournment. Beyond the board lies the state Property Tax Commission, with 30 days from the mailed decision to file. Revaluation-year boards finish by December 1.

Gather nearby sales and repair estimates first. If the appeal will outlast closing, ask your attorney about handling a later change.

Three state programs are available: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. Eligible groups are low-income owners 65 or older, low-income owners who are 100 percent disabled, and owners with a total, permanent service-connected disability (or their unmarried surviving spouses).

The state sets the dollar terms: a 2026 income limit of $38,800 on the state form, a $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, and a circuit breaker that defers part of the bill as a lien. An owner may use only one program.

The application deadline is June 1. Late applications may be considered for good cause such as illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment or delayed disability certification. Forgetting is not accepted.

The debt stays with the parcel. State law attaches the lien as of the listing date for the tax year, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure action.

At closing, the attorney gets the amount due from Tax Administration and pays it from your proceeds. Interest starts January 6, so settle before then if you can.

With an inherited house in arrears, call Tax Administration first and ask what options remain. A cash buyer will still expect the tax payoff to come out of your proceeds, but you skip a lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the payoff figure is often the main item to settle before closing.

faqs.q: Until when can I pay Wake County tax interest-free?
faqs.a: January 5, 2027 for the 2026 bills. Interest begins the next day.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Wake County bill in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes, in any amount, without approval, as long as the bill is paid by January 5. Short-term plans are available to early callers.

faqs.q: What is the next Wake County revaluation date?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027, after the January 1, 2024 cycle. Later ones follow every two years.

faqs.q: Who answers Wake County tax questions?
faqs.a: Tax Administration, 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov. For revaluation, call 919-857-3800 or email revaluation@wake.gov.

faqs.q: Do older or disabled Wake owners get relief?
faqs.a: Yes: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. The deadline is June 1.
